JP-N1-01-001.notes: が早いか means 'the instant': 帰るが早いか 'the instant (the child) got home'. It's narrative and describes someone else's sudden action; the dictionary form is used even for past events.
JP-N1-01-001.tip: が早いか, や否や, なり: all 'the instant', all narrative.
JP-N1-01-001.tr: The instant the child got home, they went out to play.
JP-N1-01-001.flag: tr: 子ども doesn't specify a boy; 'he' replaced with 'they'

JP-N1-01-002.notes: 鳴るが早いか 'the instant the bell rang': the students dash out at once. 飛び出す = rush out. The pattern suits lively descriptions of crowds or children.

JP-N1-01-003.notes: や否や means 'as soon as': 聞くや否や. It's literary; the shorter や alone is also used (聞くや). The second action follows immediately.

JP-N1-01-004.notes: 発売されるや否や 'as soon as it was released'. The passive verb takes や否や in its dictionary form. 売り切れる = sell out.

JP-N1-01-005.notes: なり means 'as soon as (and then something unexpected)': 見るなり泣き出した. It describes someone else; the speaker's own actions don't take なり.
JP-N1-01-005.tip: なり: about others, with a surprising result.

JP-N1-01-006.notes: 帰ってくるなり寝てしまった 'went straight to bed the moment he got home'. てしまう adds that this was unexpected or mildly regrettable.

JP-N1-01-007.notes: そばから means 'no sooner … than', for something that keeps happening: 覚えるそばから忘れる. The repeated frustration is the point.
JP-N1-01-007.tip: そばから = no sooner…, again and again.

JP-N1-01-008.notes: 片付けるそばから散らかす 'no sooner do I tidy than they mess it up'. It's a classic parent's complaint. 散らかす = make a mess.

JP-N1-01-009.notes: てからというもの means 'ever since', stressing a big change: 生まれてからというもの. The change has continued up to now.
JP-N1-01-009.tip: てからというもの = ever since (a big change).

JP-N1-01-010.notes: 出会ってからというもの 'ever since I met her'. The main clause describes the new, lasting state: 毎日が楽しい. 出会う = meet (by chance or fate).

JP-N1-01-011.notes: を限りに means 'as of (and never again)': 今日を限りに 'from today, for good'. It marks the last time something happens.
JP-N1-01-011.tip: を限りに = as of (the last time).

JP-N1-01-012.notes: 本日を限りに閉店いたします 'we close for good as of today'. It's a typical notice when a shop shuts down; いたす is humble.

JP-N1-01-013.notes: を皮切りに means 'starting with (the first of a series)': 東京公演を皮切りに. 皮切り literally means the first cut or moxa burn.
JP-N1-01-013.tip: を皮切りに = beginning with (the first of many).

JP-N1-01-014.notes: 発言を皮切りに 'starting with his remark'. 次々と (one after another) shows the series that followed. 反対意見 = opposing views. It's typical of reports on meetings.

JP-N1-01-015.notes: かたわら means 'while also (alongside main work)': 勤めるかたわら小説を書く. It describes a long-term side activity.
JP-N1-01-015.tip: かたわら = alongside (a main occupation).

JP-N1-01-016.notes: 子育てのかたわら 'while raising children'. Nouns take の. Unlike ながら, it isn't about two actions at the same moment.

JP-N1-01-017.notes: がてら means 'while (also), on the way': 散歩がてら. The first activity is the main one; the second is fitted in.
JP-N1-01-017.tip: がてら = combining (the trip with a second task).

JP-N1-01-018.notes: 送りがてら 'while seeing (a guest) off'. Verb stems and nouns take がてら. 送る here means accompanying someone.

JP-N1-01-019.notes: ともなれば means 'once it comes to (a higher level)': 大学生ともなれば. Natural expectations change at that level.
JP-N1-01-019.tip: ともなると / ともなれば = once it gets to (that level).

JP-N1-01-020.notes: 十二月ともなると 'once it's December'. The main clause describes what naturally happens then. にぎやか = lively, bustling. The approach of the year's end changes the mood of the streets.

JP-N1-02-001.notes: ゆえに means 'because of' in formal writing: 貧しさゆえに. It's old-fashioned and found in essays and literature.

JP-N1-02-002.notes: ゆえの before a noun: 若さゆえの失敗 'a mistake born of youth'. The noun names the result of the cause. 失敗 = failure, mistake.

JP-N1-02-003.notes: とあって means 'because (of this special situation)': 連休とあって. It's typical of news reports about crowds and events.
JP-N1-02-003.tip: とあって = since it's (a special occasion).

JP-N1-02-004.notes: 人気歌手が来るとあって 'with a popular singer coming'. The main clause describes the natural result: the venue was packed.

JP-N1-02-005.notes: ばこそ means 'precisely because': 愛していればこそ. It's a literary からこそ and introduces a reason that may seem surprising.
JP-N1-02-005.tip: ばこそ = literary からこそ.

JP-N1-02-006.notes: あればこそ 'precisely because (you are)': 健康であればこそ. The main clause often ends with のだ. 健康 here takes である: 健康であれば. The pattern praises a basic condition.

JP-N1-02-007.notes: 手前 means 'in front of (to save face)': 子どもの手前 'in front of the children'. The speaker can't act freely because others are watching.
JP-N1-02-007.tip: 手前 = because others are watching.

JP-N1-02-008.notes: 言った手前 'having said so'. Having committed in public, backing out would mean losing face. 今さら = now, at this late stage.

JP-N1-02-009.notes: こととて means 'because' in a formal apology: 慣れぬこととて. 慣れぬ is the old negative of 慣れる. It's very old-fashioned.

JP-N1-02-010.notes: 子どものしたこととて 'as it was a child's doing'. The excuse asks for forgiveness: どうかお許しください. Both こととて and the request are humble: the speaker is asking for leniency.

JP-N1-02-011.notes: にかこつけて means 'using X as an excuse': 仕事にかこつけて. The reason given isn't the real one. 飲み会 = a drinking party, often with colleagues. 断る = decline.
JP-N1-02-011.tip: にかこつけて = on the pretext of.

JP-N1-02-012.notes: 出張にかこつけて 'using a business trip as an excuse'. The real aim, sightseeing, follows. 観光 = sightseeing. The excuse is presented with a wink rather than guilt.

JP-N1-02-013.notes: をもって means 'as of' in formal notices: 本日をもって 'as of today'. 受付 is reception or the application desk.
JP-N1-02-013.tip: をもって = as of; by means of (formal).

JP-N1-02-014.notes: をもって can also mean 'by means of': 書面をもって 'in writing'. It's typical of official letters. 書面 = in writing, a document.

JP-N1-02-015.notes: とあれば means 'if it's (for X)': 子どものためとあれば. The speaker would do anything for that reason. どんなことでも = anything at all. The noun ため (sake) goes before とあれば.
JP-N1-02-015.tip: とあれば = if it's for (X), then anything.

JP-N1-02-016.notes: 命令とあれば 'if it's an order'. The speaker accepts reluctantly: 従うしかない. 命令 = order. 従う = obey. The speaker doesn't like it but sees no alternative, which suits the reluctant tone.

JP-N1-02-017.notes: にかまけて means 'too wrapped up in X (neglecting something else)': 仕事にかまけて. The neglected thing comes next.
JP-N1-02-017.tip: にかまけて = too absorbed in (X) to…

JP-N1-02-018.notes: をいいことに means 'taking (unfair) advantage of': 先生がいないのをいいことに. It criticises the behaviour that follows.
JP-N1-02-018.tip: をいいことに = taking advantage of (critical).

JP-N1-03-001.notes: たところで means 'even if (it would be pointless)': 急いだところで間に合わない. The past form is used even for hypothetical futures.
JP-N1-03-001.tip: たところで = even if (it's no use).

JP-N1-03-002.notes: いくら説明したところで 'however much you explain'. The main clause is a negative or a pessimistic guess. The pessimism is the speaker's own judgement.

JP-N1-03-003.notes: といえども means 'even (a…)': 子どもといえども. It concedes a status but insists the rule still applies. The rule applies to everyone, children included.
JP-N1-03-003.tip: といえども = even though (one is) a…

JP-N1-03-004.notes: 専門家といえども 'even experts'. It's a formal concession, typical of essays and speeches. 間違える = make a mistake. ことはある means 'it does happen (sometimes)'.

JP-N1-03-005.notes: とはいえ means 'although, that said': 春とはいえ. It admits a fact, then qualifies it. 寒い日が続く = cold days continue. The season promises warmth, but the reality lags behind.

JP-N1-03-006.notes: 忙しいとはいえ 'busy as you are'. The second clause pushes back: you could at least get in touch. 連絡くらい = at least a message. はず shows what the speaker reasonably expects.

JP-N1-03-007.notes: であれ means 'no matter (who / what)': 誰であれ. It's formal; であろうと is a variant. 規則 = rules. The phrase is common in notices: どなたであれ (whoever you may be). であっても is the everyday form.
JP-N1-03-007.tip: Question word + であれ = no matter who / what.

JP-N1-03-008.notes: 何であろうと 'whatever (the reason)'. The main clause states an unconditional rule. 暴力 = violence. 許されない = not acceptable. It suits official statements and principles.

JP-N1-03-009.notes: ようが…まいが means 'whether or not': 降ろうが降るまいが. The volitional form and まい frame the two options. 試合は行います: the match will go ahead. It's common in event announcements.
JP-N1-03-009.tip: ようが…まいが = whether or not.

JP-N1-03-010.notes: ようと means 'no matter (what)': 何と言われようと 'whatever people say'. The passive volitional 言われよう is used. 自分の道 = one's own path.

JP-N1-03-011.notes: ものを means 'if only (regret or criticism)': 言えばいいものを. The speaker blames someone for not acting. どうして reinforces the complaint.

JP-N1-03-012.notes: 治るものを 'would get better (if only)'. The second clause shows the frustrating reality: he won't take it.

JP-N1-03-013.notes: ならいざしらず means 'X would be one thing, but': 子どもならいざしらず. The real case is less forgivable. なんて ends the sentence with shock; the conclusion is left unsaid.
JP-N1-03-013.tip: ならいざしらず = (that) would be one thing, but…

JP-N1-03-014.notes: 初めてならいざしらず 'if it were the first time, fine'. The complaint follows: still wrong on the third try. 三回目 = the third time.

JP-N1-03-015.notes: にひきかえ means 'in contrast to', with a judgement: 兄にひきかえ. One side is better than the other. 兄 and 弟 are compared, with clear approval of the younger.
JP-N1-03-015.tip: にひきかえ = in (unfavourable) contrast to.

JP-N1-03-016.notes: 去年の暑さにひきかえ 'compared with last year's heat'. It contrasts two situations strongly. 涼しい = cool (pleasant). This summer is the favoured side of the contrast.

JP-N1-03-017.notes: をよそに means 'disregarding (others' concern)': 周囲の反対をよそに. The person carries on regardless. 周囲 = the people around him. 会社を辞める = quit a job.

JP-N1-03-018.notes: 親の心配をよそに 'ignoring his parents' worries'. 遊び歩く = go out enjoying oneself. 毎晩 = every night. The son's behaviour is presented as worrying his parents. It's typical of social commentary.

JP-N1-03-019.notes: をものともせずに means 'undaunted by': 大けがをものともせず. It admires someone's courage. 出場する = take part (in a match or competition). It's common in sports reporting, praising an athlete's grit.
JP-N1-03-019.tip: をものともせず = undaunted by.

JP-N1-03-020.notes: 嵐をものともせず 'undaunted by the storm'. It can describe things as well as people. 港を出る = leave port. The ship is personified as brave. It's typical of narrative writing.

JP-N1-03-021.notes: をおして means 'pushing through (illness, opposition)': 病気をおして. It shows determination. 出席する = attend. It's common in reports praising dedication: someone came in despite being unwell.
JP-N1-03-021.tip: をおして = in spite of (and pushing on).

JP-N1-03-022.notes: ならまだしも means 'X would be acceptable, but': 一回ならまだしも. The real situation goes too far. 何度も = again and again. 困る = be a problem.
JP-N1-03-022.tip: ならまだしも = (that) would be one thing.

JP-N1-03-023.notes: と思いきや means 'I thought…, but actually': 簡単だと思いきや. The result is the opposite of the expectation. The past とても難しかった shows the actual outcome.
JP-N1-03-023.tip: と思いきや = I expected…, but no.

JP-N1-03-024.notes: と思いきや after a past form: 合格したと思いきや 'I thought I'd passed'. The surprise follows: my name wasn't there.
JP-N1-03-024.text: (Written) 合格した{{c1::と思いきや::I thought …, but (actually)}}、名前がなかった。
JP-N1-03-024.tr: I thought I'd passed, but my name wasn't on the list.
JP-N1-03-024.flag: dup: replaced 雨がやんだと思いきや、また降り出した (near-identical to N2-01-008)

JP-N1-03-025.notes: かいもなく means 'in vain, despite': 努力したかいもなく. かい (甲斐) is the reward an effort deserves. 試験に落ちる = fail an exam. The effort was real but brought nothing.
JP-N1-03-025.tip: かいもなく = all for nothing.

JP-N1-03-026.notes: 看病のかいもなく 'despite our care'. It's typical of obituaries and sad news. 亡くなる = pass away. 看病 = nursing (a sick person). 祖父 = grandfather.

JP-N1-03-027.notes: をもってしても means 'even with (the best means)': 最新の技術をもってしても. The result is still negative. 最新の技術 = the latest technology. 治せない = cannot cure.
JP-N1-03-027.tip: をもってしても = even with (it still fails).

JP-N1-04-001.notes: ならでは means 'only N can offer': 京都ならではの味. It's always praise. だけあって means 'as you'd expect, given': プロだけあって.
JP-N1-04-001.tip: ならでは = unique to; だけあって = as expected from.

JP-N1-04-002.notes: 手作りならではの温かさ 'a warmth only handmade things have'. It's common in advertising copy. 手作り = handmade. 温かさ = warmth (of feeling).

JP-N1-04-003.notes: をおいて means 'apart from (no one else)': 彼をおいてほかにいない. It strongly singles out one choice. 任せる = entrust. ほかにいない = there's no one else. It's a strong endorsement in formal speech.
JP-N1-04-003.tip: をおいて…ない = no one but.

JP-N1-04-004.notes: あなたをおいて考えられない 'can't imagine anyone but you'. It's a strong compliment. 考えられない = unthinkable. 次のリーダー = the next leader. It's flattering and persuasive.

JP-N1-04-005.notes: に限る means 'X is the best (thing to do)': 寝るに限る. It's a personal recommendation. 疲れたとき = when you're tired. It's said with conviction, from experience.

JP-N1-04-006.notes: ビールに限ります 'nothing beats beer'. ね invites agreement. Nouns go straight before に限る. It's often said with a satisfied sigh on a hot day. The meaning is 'the best, and nothing else'.

JP-N1-04-007.notes: ないまでも means 'even if not (as far as X), at least Y': 毎日とは言わないまでも. The second part is a modest demand.
JP-N1-04-007.tip: ないまでも = not X, but at least Y.

JP-N1-04-008.notes: できないまでも 'even if we can't (win)'. The lesser goal, reaching the final, is still wanted. 優勝 = winning the championship; 決勝 = the final.

JP-N1-04-009.notes: なくして means 'without (X, Y is impossible)': 努力なくして成功はない. It's formal and typical of speeches. It's a stock phrase in motivational speeches.
JP-N1-04-009.tip: なくして(は) + negative = without (X, never).

JP-N1-04-010.notes: ご協力なくしては 'without your cooperation'. The main clause is a negative of what was achieved. 実現 = realisation, making it happen.

JP-N1-04-011.notes: なしに means 'without': 断りなしに 'without asking'. It's a neutral 'without'. 断り = notice, permission. 入ってくる = come in. It's critical of rude behaviour.

JP-N1-04-012.notes: ことなしに after a verb: 努力することなしに. It's more formal than ないで. 夢をかなえる = make a dream come true. ことなしに is formal, typical of speeches and essays about effort.

JP-N1-04-013.notes: が最後 means 'once you do X, that's it': 貸したが最後. The bad result can't be undone. 返ってくる = come back. 絶対に + negative = never.
JP-N1-04-013.tip: たが最後 = once you…, it's over.

JP-N1-04-014.notes: 読み始めたが最後 'once you start'. It can be humorous: you won't be able to stop. やめられなくなる = become unable to stop. It's also used as a recommendation for gripping books.

JP-N1-04-015.notes: ずとも means 'even without': 言わずとも 'without (you) having to say'. It's literary for なくても. わかっている = I already know.
JP-N1-04-015.tip: ずとも = literary なくても.

JP-N1-04-016.notes: 急がずとも 'even without hurrying'. する becomes せずとも. 間に合う = be in time. The literary ずとも sounds calm and reassuring. Everyday speech: 急がなくても間に合う.

JP-N1-04-017.notes: 限りだ after a feeling adjective means 'I feel so…': さびしい限りです. It's the speaker's own emotion. 帰ってしまう = go home (and leave me). The feeling is personal.
JP-N1-04-017.tip: Feeling + 限りだ = I feel so…

JP-N1-04-018.notes: うれしい限りです 'absolutely delighted'. It's a stock phrase in acceptance speeches. 賞 = award. いただけて is the humble potential of もらう.

JP-N1-04-019.notes: に至るまで means 'right through to': 子どもからお年寄りに至るまで. It stresses the full extent, often with から. お年寄り = the elderly.
JP-N1-04-019.tip: から…に至るまで = from … right through to.

JP-N1-05-001.notes: 極まりない means 'extremely' (usually negative): 失礼極まりない. Despite the ない, it's an intensifier, not a negative.
JP-N1-05-001.tip: 極まりない = extremely (not a negative).

JP-N1-05-002.notes: 迷惑極まりない 'incredibly inconsiderate'. 極まる (without ない) means the same. 夜中 = the middle of the night. The noun 迷惑 (nuisance) goes before 極まりない. The tone is indignant.

JP-N1-05-003.notes: の至り means 'the height of': 光栄の至り 'a great honour'. It's a fixed phrase in speeches. このような = such (formal).
JP-N1-05-003.tip: 光栄の至り = a great honour.

JP-N1-05-004.notes: 若気の至り 'the folly of youth'. It excuses past behaviour. 若気 (わかげ) = youthful impetuousness. The phrase is fixed; other nouns rarely take の至り except 光栄 and 感激.

JP-N1-05-005.notes: といったらない means 'indescribably': 怖さといったらなかった. The noun names the feeling. 夜道 = a road at night. The past ありませんでした describes a past experience.
JP-N1-05-005.tip: Noun + といったらない = beyond words.

JP-N1-05-006.notes: うれしさといったらありません 'joy beyond words'. The polite form ends in ありません. うれしさ is the noun of うれしい. Other emotion nouns fit too: 悔しさ, 寒さ. The tone is lively and spoken.

JP-N1-05-007.notes: にたえない after 見る / 聞く means 'too awful to watch / hear': 見るにたえない. 番組 = TV programme. 内容 = content. The meaning is 'too awful to look at', not 'unbearable to wait for'.

JP-N1-05-008.notes: 感謝にたえない means 'deeply grateful': the feeling can't be contained. It's very formal. 支援 = support. It's said at award ceremonies.

JP-N1-05-009.notes: にもまして means 'even more than': 去年にもまして暑い. The noun goes straight before にもまして. 暑い is the quality that has increased. It's common in weather reports and essays.
JP-N1-05-009.tip: 何にもまして = more than anything.

JP-N1-05-010.notes: 何にもまして 'more than anything'. It introduces the top priority. 健康が大切 = health matters. The phrase sets a clear priority over everything else.

JP-N1-05-011.notes: からある after a number means 'as much as (a lot)': 百キロからある荷物. 荷物 = luggage, load. 一人で = alone. The number is presented as remarkably large for one person to carry.
JP-N1-05-011.tip: Number + から(ある) = a good (number).

JP-N1-05-012.notes: からの before a noun: 一万人からの人 'as many as 10,000 people'. 集まる = gather. The number of people impresses the speaker. It's typical of news reports about rallies and festivals.

JP-N1-05-013.notes: たりとも means 'not even (one)': 一円たりとも. It takes a negative. 無駄にする = waste. The emphasis shows strict economy. It's typical of budgets and determined speech.
JP-N1-05-013.tip: 一 + counter + たりとも + negative.

JP-N1-05-014.notes: 一日たりとも 'not even a single day'. The verb is negative: 休んだことはない. 練習を休む = miss practice. The past ことはない means 'have never'. It shows great dedication.

JP-N1-05-015.notes: すら means 'even (a basic thing)': 名前すら書けない. It's a written さえ. 自分の名前 = one's own name. The basic thing is singled out to show how little he can do.

JP-N1-05-016.notes: だに means 'even (just)': 想像するだに恐ろしい. It's literary and survives in a few phrases. 恐ろしい = terrifying. It's mostly with 想像する, 考える.

JP-N1-05-017.notes: にして means 'only at (that point) did': 四十歳にして初めて. It stresses how late or high the point is. 初めて = for the first time.
JP-N1-05-017.tip: にして = only at; even (someone like).

JP-N1-05-018.notes: にして can mean 'even (an expert)': 専門家にして解けない. 解けない = can't solve. The expert's failure shows how hard the problem is. そうです marks hearsay. It's written in tone.

JP-N1-05-019.notes: までだ means 'I'll just (have to) do it': 歩いて帰るまでです. It's calm resignation. The condition (no trains) is stated first with なら.

JP-N1-05-020.notes: までのことだ after a past form: 答えたまでのことです 'I merely answered'. It plays down an action. 聞かれた = was asked. The speaker denies any further motive.

JP-N1-05-021.notes: ばそれまでだ means 'once X, that's the end': 死んでしまえばそれまで. いくら…ても = however much. The proverb-like idea is that money can't be taken with you.
JP-N1-05-021.tip: ばそれまでだ = once that happens, it's all over.

JP-N1-05-022.notes: 使わなければそれまで 'pointless if you don't use it'. 高い = expensive. Owning isn't enough; use gives value. The ば form 使わなければ is the negative condition.

JP-N1-05-023.notes: てまで means 'go so far as to': 借金をしてまで. The action is too extreme. 借金 = debt. The speaker refuses to go to such lengths. It's common in moral judgements: うそをついてまで.
JP-N1-05-023.tip: てまで = going as far as (doing something extreme).

JP-N1-05-024.notes: とて means 'even (X, like everyone)': 私とて. It's literary for でも / だって. 悲しくないわけではない = it's not that I'm not sad. The double negative expresses quiet emotion.

JP-N1-06-001.notes: ずにはおかない says a thing inevitably makes others feel or do something: 観客を感動させずにはおかない. ずにはいられない is your own urge: 感動せずにはいられなかった.
JP-N1-06-001.tip: ずにはおかない = bound to make (others)…; ずにはいられない = I can't help.

JP-N1-06-002.notes: 考えさせずにはおかない 'can't fail to make (them) think'. The subject is the film, acting on its viewers. It's typical of reviews.

JP-N1-06-003.notes: ずにはすまない means 'can't get away without (doing)': 弁償せずにはすまない. The situation, not an inner urge, demands it. する becomes せずに.
JP-N1-06-003.tip: ずにはすまない = it can't be left without…

JP-N1-06-004.notes: 報告せずにはすみません 'can't avoid reporting it'. It's a social or professional obligation that can't be dodged.

JP-N1-06-005.notes: を禁じ得ない means 'can't help feeling': 同情を禁じ得ない. It's very formal and goes with feeling nouns: 同情, 怒り, 驚き, 涙.
JP-N1-06-005.tip: を禁じ得ない = can't suppress (a feeling).

JP-N1-06-006.notes: 怒りを禁じ得ません 'can't help feeling angry'. 判決 is a court verdict. The phrase suits editorials and statements.

JP-N1-06-007.notes: を余儀なくされる means 'be forced to (by circumstances)': 中止を余儀なくされた. The subject had no choice. It's standard in news.
JP-N1-06-007.tip: を余儀なくされる = be forced (by circumstances).

JP-N1-06-008.notes: 入院を余儀なくされました 'was forced into hospital'. The cause comes first: 病気で. The phrase removes any sense of choice.

JP-N1-06-009.notes: べく means 'in order to' in writing: 実現するべく努力する. する becomes するべく or すべく. It shows strong purpose. 夢を実現する = make a dream come true.
JP-N1-06-009.tip: べく = in order to; べからず = must not.
JP-N1-06-009.text: 夢を{{c1::実現するべく::実現する · べく / べからず / べくもない?}}、毎日努力しています。
JP-N1-06-009.flag: hint: added '?' to the option list so the card counts as Choice

JP-N1-06-010.notes: べからず means 'must not', on signs and in rules: 芝生に入るべからず 'keep off the grass'. It's old-fashioned and stern.
JP-N1-06-010.text: (A sign) 芝生に{{c1::入るべからず::入る · べく / べからず / べくもない?}}。
JP-N1-06-010.flag: hint: added '?' to the option list so the card counts as Choice

JP-N1-06-011.notes: べくもない means 'there's no way to (can't even hope)': 及ぶべくもない 'can't hope to match'. 私など is modest: someone like me.
JP-N1-06-011.text: 彼の実力には、私など{{c1::及ぶべくもありません::及ぶ · べく / べからず / べくもない?}}。
JP-N1-06-011.flag: hint: added '?' to the option list so the card counts as Choice

JP-N1-06-012.notes: にかたくない means 'it isn't hard to': 想像にかたくない 'easy to imagine'. かたい here means 'difficult', not 'hard (solid)'.
JP-N1-06-012.tip: 想像にかたくない = easy to imagine.

JP-N1-06-013.notes: 察するにかたくない 'easy to understand (someone's feelings)'. 察する = sense, sympathise with. The pattern goes with only a few verbs.

JP-N1-06-014.notes: に足る means 'worthy of': 信頼に足る人物 'a trustworthy person'. It's formal and goes before a noun. 人物 = a person (of character).
JP-N1-06-014.tip: に足る = worthy of; 取るに足りない = trivial.

JP-N1-06-015.notes: 取るに足りない means 'trivial, not worth bothering about'. It's a fixed negative phrase built on 足る. 問題 = issue.

JP-N1-06-016.notes: てやまない means 'never cease to (wish, hope)': 願ってやみません. It's the stock ending of formal speeches and letters.
JP-N1-06-016.tip: てやまない = never cease to (formal).

JP-N1-06-017.notes: 愛してやまない 'never stopped loving'. It describes deep, lasting feelings, and is common in biographies and tributes.

JP-N1-06-018.notes: きらいがある means 'tend to (an undesirable habit)': 大げさに言うきらいがある. It's a polite but critical observation.
JP-N1-06-018.tip: きらいがある = has a (bad) tendency to.

JP-N1-06-019.notes: 避けるきらいがあります 'tends to avoid'. The subject can be an organisation as well as a person. 新しいこと = anything new.

JP-N1-06-020.notes: しまつだ means 'end up (after a series of bad things)': クビになるしまつ. It's critical; ついには (finally) often precedes it.
JP-N1-06-020.tip: しまつだ = it came to this (bad end).

JP-N1-06-021.notes: 留年するしまつです 'has ended up repeating a year'. とうとう (at last) marks the culmination of neglect. 留年 = repeating a school year.

JP-N1-06-022.notes: とは at the end of a clause expresses surprise: 結婚するとは 'to think they'd marry'. The reaction verb (思いもしなかった) often follows.

JP-N1-06-023.notes: 会うとは 'to think we'd meet'. The English equivalent is 'Fancy meeting you here!'. The main verb can be dropped.

JP-N1-06-024.notes: んばかり means 'as if about to': 泣き出さんばかり. とばかりに after a quote means 'as if to say': 「待ってました」とばかりに. 泣き出す → 泣き出さ + んばかり.
JP-N1-06-024.tip: んばかり = almost; とばかりに = as if to say.

JP-N1-06-025.notes: あるまじき means 'unbecoming of': 教師にあるまじき行為. It condemns behaviour unfit for a role. 行為 = act, conduct. It's typical of news reports on scandals involving teachers, police or politicians.
JP-N1-06-025.tip: にあるまじき = unbecoming of.

JP-N1-06-026.notes: 欠くべからざる means 'indispensable': 生活に欠くべからざるもの. べからざる is the attributive of べからず. 生活 = life, daily living. 欠く = lack. It's a formal, essay-like expression.

JP-N1-06-027.notes: ときたら means 'when it comes to (complaint)': うちの息子ときたら. The speaker is exasperated. ばかり + する = do nothing but. うちの息子 = my son (humble).
JP-N1-06-027.tip: ときたら = complaint; にかけては = praise.

JP-N1-06-028.notes: んがため means 'in order to' with strong resolve: 実現せんがため. する becomes せん. It's literary. 全てを捨てる = give up everything. It's dramatic and literary.
JP-N1-06-028.tip: んがため = literary ために.

JP-N1-06-029.notes: べくして means 'as was bound to happen': 起こるべくして起こった. The same verb repeats. 起こる = happen. The phrase suggests negligence made the event inevitable. It's common in commentary after disasters.
JP-N1-06-029.tip: V べくして V = bound to (and did).

JP-N1-06-030.notes: てはばからない means 'not hesitate to (say openly)': 天才だと言ってはばからない. It's usually critical. 天才 = genius. The tone mocks his self-assurance.

JP-N1-06-031.notes: AといいBといい means 'both A and B' in an evaluation: 味といい、値段といい. It typically leads to praise or criticism.
JP-N1-06-031.tip: AといいBといい = in both A and B (evaluating).

JP-N1-07-001.notes: にあって means 'in (a particular situation)': 厳しい状況にあって. It stresses how the situation shapes behaviour. It's more literary than において.
JP-N1-07-001.tip: にあって = in (a situation), given that.

JP-N1-07-002.notes: 立場にあって 'in the position of'. The role brings responsibilities: such a remark is unacceptable for someone in it.

JP-N1-07-003.notes: に即して means 'in accordance with (facts, rules)': 事実に即して. It demands close conformity to reality. 報告書 = report.
JP-N1-07-003.tip: に即して = strictly in line with.

JP-N1-07-004.notes: 法律に即して 'in accordance with the law'. It's typical of official decisions and legal commentary. 判断する = judge, decide.

JP-N1-07-005.notes: いかんで means 'depending on': 結果いかんで. It's very formal; 次第で is the everyday equivalent. 次の計画 = the next plan. The noun 結果 goes straight before いかん.
JP-N1-07-005.tip: いかんで = formal 次第で.

JP-N1-07-006.notes: いかんによらず means 'regardless of': 理由のいかんによらず 'whatever the reason'. It's common in rules and terms of service.

JP-N1-07-007.notes: をふまえて means 'taking into account, building on': 反省をふまえて. 反省 here means lessons learnt from reflection.
JP-N1-07-007.tip: をふまえて = building on (lessons, findings).

JP-N1-07-008.notes: 結果をふまえて 'based on the results'. 対策 = countermeasures. It's a staple of business reports. 調査 = survey, investigation.

JP-N1-07-009.notes: はおろか means 'let alone': 漢字はおろか、ひらがなも書けない. The more basic item comes second, with も or さえ. The basic item is ひらがな, which is easier than kanji.
JP-N1-07-009.tip: AはおろかBも = not even B, let alone A.

JP-N1-07-010.notes: 旅行はおろか 'let alone travel'. Even the simpler activity is impossible. 近所に出かける = pop out locally. The negative is on the simpler activity: 時間もない. It's typical of complaints about busy lives.

JP-N1-07-011.notes: ともなく means 'without really meaning to': 見るともなく見る 'watch idly'. The same verb is often repeated. テレビを見る is the repeated verb.
JP-N1-07-011.tip: 見るともなく見る = watch without paying attention.

JP-N1-07-012.notes: どこからともなく 'from somewhere or other'. A question word + ともなく makes the source vague. 香り = scent. してくる = start to come (towards me).

JP-N1-07-013.notes: に照らして means 'in light of, measured against': 法律に照らして. It suits judgements against a standard. 無罪 = not guilty.

JP-N1-07-014.notes: 過去の例に照らして 'in light of past cases'. 考えると completes the reasoning. 例 = example, precedent. 危険 = dangerous. It's typical of risk assessments and expert opinions.

JP-N1-07-015.notes: にかかわる means 'affecting (something serious)': 命にかかわる問題 'a matter of life and death'. 命 = life. The phrase is fixed and common.

JP-N1-07-016.notes: 信用にかかわる 'affecting (the company's) reputation'. 慎重に対応する = handle carefully. 信用 = trust, credibility. The noun goes straight before にかかわる. It's a warning in business contexts.

JP-N1-07-017.notes: と相まって means 'combined with (and reinforcing)': 好天と相まって. Two factors together produce the result. にぎわう = be bustling.

JP-N1-07-018.notes: 音楽と相まって 'combined with the music'. さらに (even more) shows the reinforcement. 感動的 = moving. Both factors push in the same direction. It's typical of reviews and essays.

JP-N1-08-001.notes: ながらに means 'from, while still': 生まれながらに 'from birth'. 涙ながらに (in tears) is another fixed use. 才能 = talent.
JP-N1-08-001.tip: 生まれながら = from birth.

JP-N1-08-002.notes: いながらにして 'while staying (at home)'. It's typical of praise for technology. いる + ながらにして = while staying put. 世界中の人 = people around the world. It emphasises convenience.

JP-N1-08-003.notes: だらけ: full of unpleasant things. まみれ: covered in a liquid or powder. ずくめ: entirely, often all good or all one colour.
JP-N1-08-003.tip: だらけ = full of; まみれ = smeared with; ずくめ = all.
JP-N1-08-003.text:
この作文は{{c1::まちがいだらけ::まちがい · だらけ / まみれ / ずくめ?}}です。
彼は{{c2::汗まみれ::汗 · だらけ / まみれ / ずくめ?}}になって働きました。
今年は{{c3::いいことずくめ::いいこと · だらけ / まみれ / ずくめ?}}の一年でした。
JP-N1-08-003.flag: hint: added '?' to the option list so the card counts as Choice

JP-N1-08-004.notes: 黒ずくめ 'all in black'. ずくめ suits colours and good fortune. 服を着る = wear clothes. ずくめ also gives いいことずくめ (nothing but good things). It describes something complete and uniform.
JP-N1-08-004.text: 彼はいつも{{c1::黒ずくめ::黒 · だらけ / まみれ / ずくめ?}}の服を着ています。
JP-N1-08-004.flag: hint: added '?' to the option list so the card counts as Choice

JP-N1-08-005.notes: めく means 'show signs of': 春めく 'feel like spring'. It conjugates as a う-verb: 春めいてきた. 日差し = sunshine.
JP-N1-08-005.tip: Noun + めく = take on (a quality).

JP-N1-08-006.notes: めいた before a noun: 皮肉めいた 'tinged with sarcasm'. It describes a hint, not the full thing. 言い方 = way of speaking.

JP-N1-08-007.notes: ごとく means 'like': 矢のごとく 'like an arrow'. It's literary for のように. 過ぎていく = pass by. The proverb 光陰矢のごとし (time flies like an arrow) uses the classical form ごとし.
JP-N1-08-007.tip: ごとく / ごとき = literary ように / ような.

JP-N1-08-008.notes: ごとき before a noun: 彼のごとき人物. It can also be dismissive: 私ごとき 'someone like me'. めったにいない = rarely found. It can be admiring here.

JP-N1-08-009.notes: たる means 'as one who is': 教師たる者. It implies the duties of the role. 手本 = model, example. The duty follows with なければならない. It sounds lofty and formal.
JP-N1-08-009.tip: Nたる者 = anyone who is an N (should…).

JP-N1-08-010.notes: たるもの means 'anyone who is (an N) must…': 医者たるもの. It's followed by a duty, often with なければならない or べきだ. It sounds lofty and moralising.
JP-N1-08-010.text: 医者{{c1::たる::as one who is}}もの、患者の秘密を守らなければならない。
JP-N1-08-010.tr: A doctor must keep patients' secrets.
JP-N1-08-010.flag: dup: replaced 政治家たるもの、約束は守るべきです (near-identical to N3-07-005)

JP-N1-08-011.notes: なりに means 'in one's own way (within one's limits)': 私なりに. It's modest. がんばってみる = try one's best. The modesty suggests the result may not be perfect. It's common in self-introductions.
JP-N1-08-011.tip: なりに = in my own (limited) way.

JP-N1-08-012.notes: なりの before a noun: 子どもなりの考え 'a child's own way of thinking'. It respects the limited view. 考え = thoughts.

JP-N1-08-013.notes: ぶる means 'put on airs, act as if': 偉ぶる 'act superior'. It's critical. 偉い = important, great. It conjugates like a う-verb: 偉ぶっている. The tone is disapproving.

JP-N1-08-014.notes: 上品ぶる 'act refined'. な-adjectives and nouns take ぶる directly. 上品 = refined, elegant. The second clause reveals the truth: 本当は違う. It's catty in tone.

JP-N1-08-015.notes: ともあろう means 'someone of such standing': 教授ともあろう人. The criticism follows: they should know better. ミス = mistake.
JP-N1-08-015.tip: ともあろう人が = someone of (such status) should know better.

JP-N1-09-001.notes: ではあるまいか means 'isn't it the case that?' in formal writing: 無理があるのではあるまいか. It's a cautious suggestion.
JP-N1-09-001.tip: のではあるまいか = written のではないだろうか.

JP-N1-09-002.notes: 知っているのではあるまいか 'couldn't it be that he knows?'. The speaker suspects but doesn't assert. 本当のこと = the truth.

JP-N1-09-003.notes: ないものでもない means 'it's not impossible': 引き受けないものでもない. It's reluctant agreement. 条件によっては = depending on the conditions. 引き受ける = take on (a job). It's a cautious, negotiating answer.
JP-N1-09-003.tip: ないものでもない = I could, if pushed.

JP-N1-09-004.notes: 間に合わないものでもない 'we might just make it'. A slim possibility exists. 急げば = if we hurry. The double negative leaves a small hope. It's more formal than 間に合うかもしれない.

JP-N1-09-005.notes: てしかるべきだ means 'ought to, would only be proper': 評価されてしかるべき 'deserves recognition'. 評価される = be recognised.
JP-N1-09-005.tip: てしかるべき = ought to (it's only proper).

JP-N1-09-006.notes: あってしかるべき 'there really ought to be'. It's a firm, formal demand. 説明 = explanation. 社員 = staff. It's a firm demand, typical of criticism of companies or governments.

JP-N1-09-007.notes: にほかならない means 'is nothing other than': ご協力にほかなりません. It's emphatic and formal. 皆様 = everyone (formal).
JP-N1-09-007.tip: にほかならない = is none other than.

JP-N1-09-008.notes: 愛情の表れにほかなりません 'nothing but a sign of love'. 表れ = expression, manifestation. 厳しさ = strictness. The pattern reinterprets something negative as positive. It's typical of essays.

JP-N1-09-009.notes: といったところだ means 'about, at most': 五十人といったところ. It suggests a modest number. 参加者 = participants. The number is presented as modest, even disappointing. It's spoken in tone.
JP-N1-09-009.tip: といったところ = about (and not more).

JP-N1-09-010.notes: 日常会話ができるといったところ 'just about good enough for everyday chat'. It's modest self-assessment. 日常会話 = everyday conversation.

JP-N1-09-011.notes: ずじまい means 'ended up never (doing)': 会えずじまい. The chance has passed. 会える → 会え + ずじまい. 結局 (in the end) is common with it. It carries regret.
JP-N1-09-011.tip: ずじまい = never got round to (and now it's too late).

JP-N1-09-012.notes: 読まずじまい 'never got round to reading'. になる (become) shows the state now. The book is still unread. 買った本 = the book I bought. It's a common confession of book lovers.

JP-N1-09-013.notes: ものと思われる means 'it is thought': impersonal and formal, typical of news reports. The speaker avoids personal responsibility.
JP-N1-09-013.tip: ものと思われる = it is thought (impersonal).

JP-N1-09-014.notes: 上陸するものと思われます 'is expected to make landfall'. 九州 is Japan's southernmost main island. 台風 = typhoon. It's a forecast phrase.
